LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  September 24, 2019
1. A regular meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by
  Mayor Don Kendrick at 6:30 p.m.

2. Executive Board Members present:

  Executive Board
  Robin Carder, Council Member
  Matthew Lyons, BUSD
  Carolyn Cockrell, BUSD
  Denise Fisher, Resident

  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Eric Podley, BUSD
  Thomas Gutierrez, BUSD
  Patti Latourelle, Resident
  Denise Fisher, Resident
  Jason Lorge, Resident
  Ron Serven, Resident
  Vanessa Hess, Resident
  David Svatos, Resident
  Krista Chakmak, Resident
  Mark Ramos, Resident
  Lacy Flippin, Fairplex
  Sam Gonzalez, LVPD
  Hollie Savage, LVPD
  Francisco Cambero, LVPD
  Halie Deguzman, Project Sister
  David Yim, Tri-City
  Sara Rodriguez, Tri-City
  Jessica Vozella, American Lung Association
  Isabella Alva, American Lung Association
  Bill Aguirre, City of La Verne
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne

  After self-introductions, Council Member Carder
  noted that the Mayor was unavailable as the result of
  a prior commitment and that she would be chairing
  the meeting.

3. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the August 27th meeting were approved.

4. Summer Lunch  Council Member Carder introduced Peggy Tomita,
  Director of Children’s Ministry for La Verne Heights
  Presbyterian. Peggy informed the group of the
  special activities that children of the church have
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes September 24, 2019, page 2

  been doing including giving weekly to support the
  City of La Verne's Summer Lunch Program. The
  collection method was especially creative with faux
  milk cartons that showed information on the lunch
  program. The children introduced themselves and
  presented a check to YFAC totaling over $200.

5. School Resource Officer  School Resource Officer (SRO) Frankie Cambero
  noted that despite the higher volume of incidents
  occurring the first week of school, things had settled
  down. After looking back at previous information,
  incidents overall are trending lower this year. The
  group discussed the likely impact messaging and
  education was having especially as it related to the
  decrease in vaping.

6. Pomona Cannabis Shops  JR Ranells with the City of La Verne shared
  information for an upcoming Pomona Planning
  Commission Hearing related to establishing zoning
  for potential cannabis shops. The ordinance and
  draft zoning would allow for shops to open near
  La Verne’s borders. The La Verne City Council acted
  to not allow these types of businesses to open in
  La Verne. Since similar issues have been important
  to YFAC previously, such as cannabis billboard
  locations, adult beverages targeting youth via
  labeling, etc…..the item was agenized to inquire if
  YFAC wanted staff to draft a letter requesting
  Pomona to consider La Verne’s border as a sensitive
  use. If La Verne’s border was considered as a
  sensitive use, these types of businesses would be
  prohibited within 1000 feet of La Verne’s border.

  Resident Mark Ramos provided detailed information
  on the background of Pomona’s ordinance noting his
  association with employee unions and working with
  Pomona officials on its creation. Mark shared
  information on the serious dangers related to illegal
  cannabis shop operations and the need for a safer
  alternative for those that will ultimately use cannabis
  because of its legality in California. BUSD and YFAC
  Board Member Matthew Lyons noted his concerns
  with YFAC sending such a letter when the issue was
  within Pomona’s boundary of influence and wanted
  additional information on what the La Verne
  community thought on the topic. The group entered
  into a lengthy discussion. Ultimately, the YFAC
  Executive Board approved a motion for staff to draft a
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes September 24, 2019, page 3

  letter requesting Pomona to consider La Verne’s
  boundary as a sensitive use.

7. School Counseling  David Yim with Tri-City’s noted that the respective
  MOU has been signed and that they were targeting
  October 9th to be in schools providing services.

8. Therapeutic Garden  Sara Rodriguez with Tri-City’s shared information on
  the Therapeutic Community Garden with the group.
  Sara also brought some items grown in the garden
  that attendees were able to take and use including
  apples and fresh herbs.

9. Round Table  Hollie Savage with the Police Department shared
  information on the upcoming November 2nd Public
  Safety Open House. Hollie noted that YFAC could
  have an informational booth and possibly hand out
  materials and the “Drive Like Your Children Live Here”
  signs. In order to consider formally, Bill Aguirre will
  work with Hollie on the details and possibly bring back
  for the next agenda.

  Frankie Cambero shared his personal feelings of
  YFAC needing to support efforts such as the letter to
  the City of Pomona regarding cannabis shops.

  YFAC Board Member Carolyn Cockrell shared
  information she had come across regarding youth cell
  phone usage and noted that she would get a copy to
  JR to send to the group.

  David Yim handed out information related to the Tri-
  City’s Stakeholder meetings taking place on October
  9th and October 10th.

  Eric Podley with the BUSD informed the group of
  recent class visits providing education to students on
  things such as vaping. Eric also updated the group on
  the Glen Davis construction progress.

  YFAC Board Member Matt Lyons noted his recent
  participation with the Principal for a Day event. Matt
  also noted his desire for additional focus on efforts to
  eradicate illegal cannabis operations and vaping
  establishments.

  Jessica Vozella with the American Lung Association
  informed the group that they were looking for youth
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes September 24, 2019, page 4

  workers and volunteers. Jessica also shared
  information on upcoming events.

  Mark Rodgers with the BUSD shared that the youth
  counseling program was under way and that the case
  load for counselors was continuing to grow. Mark also
  provided information on efforts related to suicide
  protocol, awareness, and prevention.

  Halie Deguzman with Project Sister provided
  information on her organization and its programs.

  Resident David Svatos shared that he appreciated the
  discussions and information YFAC meetings provide.

  Lacy Flippin with Fairplex provided information on the
  Youth Ambassador Volunteer Program and how
  people 15 years and older can apply to assist with
  events such as the LA County Fair, the Upland Lemon
  Festival, and other associated Fairplex events.

  Resident Jason Lorge noted that he also recently
  participated in the Principal of the Day program at
  Ramona and that the experience has furthered his
  appreciation for BUSD.

  Resident Ron Serven shared his appreciation for the
  group as well as his perspective of mindfulness. Ron
  also noted the importance of programs encouraging
  the community to avoid substances that alter reality.

10.  Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting is scheduled for October 22,
  2019 at 6:30 p.m.

11. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 7:44 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

JR Ranells
Personnel Officer
